title: Document-grounded drafting capstone

sources.finding: invoke surfaces __interrupt__; resume with Command and the same thread_id; an interrupted node restarts, so separate approval from file side effects.
ChatAnthropic supports bind_tools and standardized AIMessage.tool_calls; return a ToolMessage matching the call ID.
A tool name forces that tool; parallel_tool_calls=False disables parallel calls. The capstone still validates exactly one call.
DefaultEmbeddingFunction uses local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings and may automatically download model files on first use.
Related source Drafter introduction, 02:28:46; C01 is an added capstone, not a video assignment.
Related source RAG introduction, 02:52:09; local embeddings, Anthropic generation and checkpoint approval are course adaptations.
Some current models reject forced tool choice. Search uses auto plus explicit instructions and an exactly-one-call gate; draft turns retain tools with tool_choice none.
Client tools run in the application, and the next request returns matching tool_result blocks while retaining tool definitions.

limitations: Development runs offline tests only; parent must validate real Anthropic, Chroma/ONNX download, tracing and screenshots.
Requires L11 course_support.retrieval and data/rag_* teaching fixtures; helper is imported lazily, never replaced with a fake live retrieval implementation.
InMemorySaver isolates threads within one process; this capstone does not claim restart-durable checkpoints.
Citation checks validate references against retrieved source/page metadata, not semantic entailment; a human must inspect the draft.
One retrieval call, at most one revision and three model calls per successful thread; no retry loop for malformed model output.
safe_write_text prevents overwrite but is not a transactional exactly-once save across process crashes.
CLI run_demo is a scripted teaching driver: it explicitly supplies review decisions; an external UI must authenticate its real approver.
Windows execution and dashboard trace ingestion are not validated by this module author.
